phenol.point: Deepak Phenolics is India's largest phenol and acetone maker (>50% share of both); the rest of demand is met by imports and Hindustan Organic Chemicals (HOCL).

Phenol is a globally traded commodity: Indian prices track import parity (Asian prices plus freight and duty). Chinese capacity additions collapsed Asian margins in FY26 and forced shutdowns of inefficient Asian plants (DPL chairman's letter).

Middle East war (Q4FY26-Q1FY27) disrupted feedstock and freight; India waived customs duty on phenol and other petrochemicals from 2-Apr to 30-Jun-2026 (Notification 12/2026-Customs); management says duty was reimposed afterwards.

Spreads: Phenolics EBIT/kg rose to ₹21.5 in Q1FY27 from ₹16.5 in Q4FY26 (PL); PL says phenol-acetone spreads 'have already begun moderating on a week-on-week basis' and that global phenol overcapacity 'remains a structural concern'.

New domestic competition: Haldia Petrochemicals' ₹6,000 cr phenol-acetone complex (subsidiary Adperma) was due to start in October 2026; planned at 300 ktpa phenol in 2023 and upsized to 345 ktpa through a Lummus licence amendment. That is close to DPL's own ~350-400 ktpa.
Management (Aug-2026): 'no new capacities are coming up… there is a short supply today.' This does not square with Haldia's plant, due weeks later.

intermediates.point: Chinese oversupply in nitration chemistries cut AI realisations: AI revenue fell from ₹3,034 cr (FY23) to ~₹2,400 cr run-rate, 'a substantial amount… because of pricing'.
China announced tighter controls on hazardous chemistries (production, storage, transport) in Dec-2025; management says the tailwind for nitration has 'already started happening'.

US anti-dumping duty on Indian sodium nitrite cut from ~45-48% to essentially zero and the US reciprocal tariff on India cut from 50% to 18% (early 2026); DN exported ~5,000 t a year to the US before.

polycarbonate.point: India imports >300,000 t a year of polycarbonate resin (management, Feb-2026; ~4,00,000 t including compounds per the FY26 annual report) and has no domestic resin maker.
PL (Apr-2026) downgraded DN to Reduce on the view that global capacity additions threaten polycarbonate margins.

moat.evidence: >50% share; world-scale Dahej complex run at ~165% of original capacity after ₹80-100 cr of debottlenecking; best-in-class product quality (management).
Prices follow import parity; feedstock (benzene, propylene) bought at market; Petronet propylene pipeline (15 years, 250 ktpa) only from the phenol-2 era.
Phenolics EBITDA margin swung from 28% (FY21) to 14% (FY23-26) and back to ~25% (Q1FY27) with global spreads; China and now Haldia set the marginal price.
India's largest sodium nitrite maker; top-3 globally in xylidines and oximes; long qualification cycles (OBA took 24+ months with detergent majors).
AI EBIT fell from ₹596 cr (FY22) to ₹107 cr (FY26) as Chinese pricing hit; AI segment pre-tax ROCE 4.8% in FY26.

moat.dimension: Integration (ammonia → nitric acid → nitration → amines; benzene/propylene → phenol → MIBK/PC)
moat.evidence: Real cost and supply-security benefits, but the nitric acid plant ran at ~45% in Q4FY26 and the PC chain is not yet built.
1,500+ customers; 'Depend on Deepak' just-in-time supply to Indian SMEs who cannot hold import parcels; PC compounds qualified with Mahindra, Panasonic, Tata AutoComp.
ICRA AA (Stable); net debt ₹1,156 cr at Mar-2026, but rising to ~₹7,000-8,000 cr by FY29 on the PC programme.
